comments: Can confirm same error on Linux.

I've verified that the argument bins here needs to be changed to an int but is still a string when `auto` is passed:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/hist.py#L42-L63

`_args_adjust` can take care of that when called:

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/master/pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/hist.py#L25-L40

Working on a PR.

review_comments: Is there a particular reason that we have a separate call to `np.histogram` above to get the bins? Is it not possible to return the appropriate values from the `ax.hist` call here?

`cls._initialize_stacker` needs the number of bins. `ax.hist` can't provide that yet, since it needs `bottom`, which comes from `cls._get_stacked_values` and that can't be called before `cls._initialize_stacker`. That's my understanding.
Can you write a test that actually ensures the binning behavior of "auto", i.e. not just that this works without error but that it also actually provides back the correct bin values?
Are you asking me to check that `np.histogram` works? Should I also check every possible valid string that `np.histogram` takes?
Not asking to check `np.histogram` but rather that the plot renders the ticklabels of the rendered plot are as expected. I think can just use `get_xticklabels` to be sure

Honestly not sure how to go about this other than manually creating a couple of histograms and just checking the locations of the bins. The xtick labels could be the same for a histogram that uses "auto" and one that doesn't. For example:

```
df = DataFrame(randn(1000))
df.hist(bins="auto")
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5508833/76103995-9fe1c180-5fa0-11ea-884f-b96fd15b1d99.png)
```
df.hist()
```
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5508833/76104009-a40ddf00-5fa0-11ea-8a95-4301753bb862.png)
I think that's fine; even just checking for those labels would improve the test, knowing they don't stray from the default
Why is this necessary? Why can we just pass the string to matplotlib?

The comment above it explains why - we need the value of bins to be a list of bin locations and not a string because it is used in creating stackers here: https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/129b62fbe8e2aa153ecdaccdcc14a8846e430060/pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/hist.py#L59-L62

The results from initializing the stacker are also required to create the plot (specifically the argument `bottom` which is calculated from `base` which requires `bins` to be a list of bins and not a string).
Matplotlib returns `bins` from `hist`. Can we pass it the string capture that?

You're correct that it returns bins (2nd arg here):

https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blob/129b62fbe8e2aa153ecdaccdcc14a8846e430060/pandas/plotting/_matplotlib/hist.py#L65

But that needs `bottom`. `bottom` needs `base` and `base` needs `bins` to be a list not a string (see lines above).
